chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Talhah ibn Zayd from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: "Whoever trades without knowledge plunges into usury, then plunges again."
He said: "And the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) used to say: Let not anyone sit in the market except one who understands buying and selling."

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤِمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)

ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of trading without knowledge according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ali (AS) links commercial ignorance directly to the risk of *riba* (usury), suggesting that lack of expertise leads to accidental exploitation or debt traps. The hadith further prescribes that market participation should be restricted to those who possess *fiqh* (jurisprudential understanding) of transactional mechanics, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on integrating legal knowledge with economic practice to ensure justice in trade.
